question: The number of prime numbers lying between 393 and 401, both included, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

List the odd numbers from 393 to 401: 393, 395, 397, 399, 401.

Eliminate 395 (ends in 5) and multiples of 3 (393 and 399, as their digit sum is divisible by 3).

The only remaining possible primes are 397 and 401.

Check their divisibility by primes up to 19 (since √401 ≈ 20).

Neither 397 nor 401 is divisible by 7, 11, 13, 17, or 19, meaning both are prime numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers lying between 393 and 401 (inclusive).

**Method Used:**

Filter out the composite numbers using standard divisibility rules (by 2, 3, and 5) and verify the remaining numbers using the prime divisibility test up to √N.

**Calculations:**

⇒ The list of numbers to evaluate: 393, 394, 395, 396, 397, 398, 399, 400, 401

⇒ Eliminate the even numbers (divisible by 2): 394, 396, 398, 400

⇒ Eliminate the numbers ending in 5 (divisible by 5): 395

⇒ Eliminate the numbers whose digit sum is a multiple of 3: 393 (sum = 15) and 399 (sum = 21)

⇒ The only numbers left to verify are 397 and 401.

⇒ Check 397: √397 ≈ 19.9. Prime numbers ≤ 19 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19.

⇒ 397 is not exactly divisible by any of these primes, making 397 a prime number.

⇒ Check 401: √401 ≈ 20.0. Prime numbers ≤ 19 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19.

⇒ 401 is not exactly divisible by any of these primes, making 401 a prime number.

⇒ The prime numbers in the given range are exactly two (397 and 401).

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Number Test

To check if a number N is prime, find the approximate square root of N. Test its divisibility by all prime numbers less than or equal to √N. If none divide it completely, then N is a prime number.

Twin Primes

Twin primes are a pair of prime numbers that differ by exactly 2. Common examples include (3, 5), (11, 13), and (41, 43).

Co-Prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime (or mutually prime) if they do not share any common factor other than 1. Their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is always exactly 1.
